title: Sprint planning gives a code item a check that runs its behaviour, with the test it extends in touches
goal: kb-sprint plan (steps 2 and 6) and kb/_self/backlog.md Sprints say that a committed item whose touches name code under _tools/ has at least one check that runs the changed behaviour (a test selection it extends, or the tool run on a planted input), not only a read of source text, and that the test file it extends is in its touches before the start gate; a check that reads clone or host state a hand run can satisfy (refs, files outside the tree, a spool) is paired with one that runs the code path the goal names; a check that bounds a tool's git calls counts every git process (subprocess.Popen of git), not one helper's calls; an item that adds or widens a cache carries a check that changing each input, including the computing code, gives a fresh value; a check that asserts a phrase's absence reads only the line or section the goal names, not the whole file; a goal that attributes rows or windows around a landing gets one check that drives the land sequence (rebase, done --commit, a failing step) on a fixture, not a hand-set item file. backlog.py check warns of an open item in a planned sprint whose touches name _tools/ code and whose every check only reads files (the warning says its checks only read files), and of a _tools/test_*.py file its notes or goal name that no touch covers (naming the file and set ID --add-touch). Answers the SP-gkbtjjce retrospective: ST-2zl47dfu, ST-bum7owtw, ST-idwjvloy and BG-dsab2ti3 were committed with checks that grepped bl_land.py, and ST-ocfkanth's check passed while its stderr named no worktree (BG-eam5x2q7); and ST-pvtfs43r's done was refused for _tools/test_land_e2e.py, named in notes but not in touches (SP-evkj4avq).

run:
import os, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile
T = os.path.abspath('_tools/backlog.py')
r = tempfile.mkdtemp()
subprocess.run(['git', 'init', '-q', r], check=True)
def b(*a):
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, T, '--root', r, *a], cwd=r, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return p.stdout + p.stderr
def pid(p, out):
    return re.search(p + r'-\w{8}', out).group(0)
e = pid('EP', b('new', 'epic', '--title', 'E', '--goal', 'g'))
s = pid('SP', b('new', 'sprint', '--title', 'S', '--goal', 'g'))
def story(t, chk, *more):
    return pid('ST', b('new', 'story', '--title', t, '--parent', e, '--sprint', s, '--goal', 'g', '--touch', '_tools/bl_check.py', '--check', chk, *more))
rd = story('reads', "python3 -c \"import sys;sys.exit(0 if 'def' in open('_tools/bl_check.py').read() else 1)\"")
rn = story('runs', 'python3 _tools/tests.py -k backlog')
nt = story('names', 'python3 _tools/tests.py -k backlog')
b('set', nt, '--notes', 'the work adds its test to _tools/test_zzz.py')
out = b('check').splitlines()
warn = lambda i, w: any(i in l and w in l for l in out)
ok = warn(rd, 'only read') and not warn(rn, 'only read') and warn(nt, '_tools/test_zzz.py')
print('reads-only code item warned, running item not, named test file warned:', ok)
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
